intro: Sikkim is a small Himalayan state between Nepal, Tibet and Bhutan, rising from river valleys at a few hundred metres to Kanchenjunga at over 8,500 metres. Khangchendzonga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, covers much of the west and north, and its trails are among the best in the eastern Himalaya.

Most adventure in Sikkim is trekking, rafting and high road trips, with paragliding near Gangtok. Permits are a bigger part of planning here than in most states, so this guide notes them for each activity. For sightseeing, stays and food, see our Sikkim travel guide.
quickAnswer: The best adventure activities in Sikkim are the Goecha La and Dzongri treks from Yuksom, the Singalila ridge trek, rafting on the Teesta and Rangit rivers, tandem paragliding near Gangtok, and road trips to Tsomgo Lake, Nathula, Zuluk and North Sikkim. The best seasons are March to May and October to December. Treks in the national park and trips to protected areas need permits, usually arranged through registered agencies.
takeaways: Goecha La is Sikkim's classic trek, eight to eleven days from Yuksom with close views of Kanchenjunga.
Rafting on the Teesta and Rangit runs outside the monsoon, with Grade II to IV rapids.
Tsomgo Lake, Nathula, Zuluk and North Sikkim need permits; foreigners need a Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim.
The October 2023 glacial lake flood on the Teesta damaged roads in North Sikkim; check access before planning.
Avoid the monsoon (June to September), when landslides often close roads.

items.name: Goecha La
body: From Yuksom, the trail climbs through rhododendron forest to Tshoka and Dzongri, then to Thangshing and Lamuney, with a pre-dawn walk towards Goecha La for sunrise on Kanchenjunga. Access beyond the first viewpoint has been restricted in recent years. Permits for Khangchendzonga National Park are arranged through registered agencies.

facts.Season: April to May, October to November

items.name: Dzongri
body: A shorter version of the Goecha La route, turning back at Dzongri after the sunrise viewpoint above camp.

items.name: Singalila ridge
body: The ridge along the Nepal border, walked from the West Bengal side via Sandakphu and Phalut, or joined from Uttarey in West Sikkim, has views of Kanchenjunga and Everest.

items.name: Monastery and village walks
body: Easier walks link the monasteries and villages of West Sikkim around Pelling, Yuksom and Ravangla.

sections.heading: Rafting on the Teesta and Rangit
paras: Rafting trips run on the Teesta and its tributary the Rangit, from points near Melli and Teesta Bazaar on the Sikkim and West Bengal border. Rapids range from Grade II to IV depending on the stretch and water level. Rafting is suspended in the monsoon.

items.name: Teesta rafting
body: Half-day trips suit beginners; longer stretches include harder rapids.

facts.Season: Outside the monsoon, about October to May

sections.heading: Paragliding near Gangtok
paras: Tandem paragliding flights near Gangtok give views over the valleys and ridges around the capital. Flights are short and depend on weather; clear mornings in spring and autumn are best.

items.name: Tsomgo Lake and Nathula
body: A glacial lake at about 3,750 metres and the Nathula border pass on the old trade route to Tibet, both reached from Gangtok with permits. Nathula is open to Indian nationals on specified days only.

items.name: Zuluk and the old silk route
body: A zig-zag road with dozens of hairpin bends climbs to Zuluk and Thambi viewpoint in East Sikkim, on the old trade route between India and Tibet.

items.name: North Sikkim
body: Lachung, Yumthang Valley and, from Lachen, Gurudongmar Lake at over 5,000 metres. The October 2023 flood on the Teesta damaged roads and bridges in the north, and access has been affected; check before planning.

sections.heading: Mountaineering
paras: The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute in Darjeeling trains its students on the Rathong glacier in West Sikkim, above Dzongri. Expedition peaks in Sikkim need permission from the Indian Mountaineering Foundation and the state.

items.name: Mountaineering courses
body: Basic and advanced courses with HMI, with field training in West Sikkim.

sections.heading: Getting there and a sample trip
paras: Bagdogra airport and New Jalpaiguri railway station in West Bengal are the gateways; Pakyong airport near Gangtok has limited flights. Gangtok is the base for East and North Sikkim, and Pelling or Yuksom for West Sikkim and the Goecha La trek.

A good week combines both: two days in Gangtok with Tsomgo Lake and paragliding, a day's drive to Pelling, and a short walk from Yuksom or a rafting trip on the Rangit on the way back to Bagdogra. Trekkers heading for Goecha La should add at least nine to eleven days.

rows: Tsomgo Lake (permit) and paragliding if the weather is clear
Rangit or Teesta rafting on the way to Bagdogra
Permit, with restrictions on some areas

safety: Acclimatise before high treks and before visiting Gurudongmar or Nathula.
Avoid travel in the monsoon, when landslides close roads for days.
Raft only with licensed operators and trained guides, outside the monsoon.
Hire trek guides through registered agencies; they arrange permits and know the trails.
Carry warm layers; even in spring, nights at Dzongri are below freezing.
packing: Warm layers and a rain jacket
Copies of ID and passport-size photos for permits

faqs.q: What are the best adventure activities in Sikkim?
faqs.a: Treks to Goecha La and Dzongri, rafting on the Teesta, paragliding near Gangtok and high road trips to Tsomgo, Zuluk and North Sikkim.

faqs.q: When is the best time for trekking in Sikkim?
faqs.a: April to May and October to November.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Goecha La?
faqs.a: Yes. Khangchendzonga National Park permits are arranged through registered trekking agencies.
Yes, with a Restricted Area Permit. Some areas, including Nathula, are closed to foreign nationals.
Access has been affected by the 2023 Teesta flood and landslides. Check current road status and permits before planning.
